column1: # mapping_set_description: 'Maps the 17 Data Fields elements (9 SBOM Metadata, 8 Component Data) of the 2026 Minimum Elements for a Software Bill of Materials (CISA et al., v2.1, 2026-07-29) to properties, classes and RelationshipType individuals of the SPDX 3.0.1 model, plus the format constructs that support three Practices and Processes elements. Follows the SPDX community implementation paper CISA 2026 minimum elements in SPDX and CycloneDX (SPDX 3.0.1 column, research verified 2026-08-07): populate the native field whose semantics match; use a documented composition (COMPOSED) only when several native constructs are needed; use a signed delivery envelope (ENVELOPE) only where SPDX has no native field (author signature). The bridge_concept column cites the bridge concept from bom.ttl shared by the source element and the SPDX field. Derived from the SPDX 3.1-dev mapping (tools/derive_spdx30.py): SPDX 3.1 is backward compatible with 3.0, so every target that exists in 3.0.1 is mapped the same way; targets added in 3.1 (Core/version, Core/intendedUse, isoAutomationLevel, byteSize, finetunedOn / pretrainedOn / validatedOn / evaluatedOn, conformsTo / Specification, SupportRelationship, ContactPointRelationship, InteractionTemplate, the Hardware profile) are replaced by the closest 3.0.1 carrier or recorded as GAP rows.'

column8: comment

NATIVE. SpdxDocument/Sbom.creationInfo.createdBy (1..*) -> Agent (Person or Organization) whose name identifies the accountable author; the generating tool goes in createdUsing, keeping author and tool distinct as CISA requires. Use the full organization name in Agent.name.

GAP (missing field) -- ENVELOPE. No SPDX version has a Core property that constitutes an author signature; verifiedUsing + Hash proves integrity only. Encapsulate the serialized SPDX document in an in-toto attestation (SPDX is a registered in-toto attestation predicate type; use the predicate URI the in-toto registry lists for the SPDX version in use) or sign with DSSE, CMS or JWS, binding signer identity, algorithm and the exact payload. narrowMatch.
The serializedInArtifact relationship links the SpdxDocument to the Artifact holding its serialized bytes; the Artifact's verifiedUsing hash is what an external signature covers. relatedMatch.

COMPOSED. The format name (SPDX) is implied by the SPDX model instance: for JSON-LD the required @context IRI (https://spdx.org/rdf/3.0.1/spdx-context.jsonld) identifies both format and version; CreationInfo.specVersion carries the precise version. No dedicated format-name field. Report the data model name, not the serialization media type (File.contentType of the serialized Artifact may additionally carry the media type).

NATIVE. CreationInfo.specVersion (1..1) = the exact SPDX specification version (e.g. '3.0.1'); a pre-release exchange should also identify the pinned ontology / schema / context revision. Distinct from the SBOM version and from component versions.

NATIVE. Software/Sbom.sbomType (0..*) with SbomType values design, source, build, analyzed, deployed, runtime describes the lifecycle context and evidence used to generate the SBOM; multiple values when evidence from several contexts is combined. Map CISA 'before build' to design/source, 'build' to build, 'after build' to analyzed/deployed/runtime. Do not use LifecycleScopedRelationship.scope as the primary mapping (it scopes individual relationships). closeMatch (value vocabulary).

NATIVE with revision rule. CreationInfo.created (1..1, Core/DateTime (UTC, second resolution) UTC, RFC 3339 profile compatible with RFC 9557) on the released Sbom/SpdxDocument. Issue a new document (new spdxId, new created) for each released correction or revision and link it with amendedBy; preserve earlier releases.
NATIVE. CreationInfo.createdUsing (0..*) -> Core/Tool; Tool.name carries the full tool name. Keep the tool separate from the author Agent in createdBy.

GAP (missing field): SPDX 3.0.1 has no Tool version property (Core/version on Tool is a 3.1 addition). Tool.name conventionally carries name and version together; alternatives are an ExternalIdentifier of type packageUrl on the Tool or a Tool -> versioned Package relationship. broadMatch (container fallback).

GAP (missing field): SPDX 3.0.1 has no SBOM-version field (Core/version on Bom is a 3.1 addition). The amendedBy relationship gives the revision lineage; a human-readable version string can only go in Element.comment on the Sbom. broadMatch (container fallback).

Revision lineage: Relationship with relationshipType amendedBy from the earlier Sbom/SpdxDocument to the revised one, mirroring the SPDX 2.x AMENDS practice. closeMatch. Note: the RelationshipType vocabulary says the from Element is amended by each to Element (previous -> new), while the Bom class text says the Relationship goes from the updated BOM to the original; the model contradicts itself.

NATIVE. Software/Package (Artifact).originatedBy (0..*) -> Agent identifies the entity that created, defined and identified the component. suppliedBy is not a substitute unless the supplier also originated the component. For unknown provenance point to the NoAssertionElement individual or omit with an explanatory comment. Organization.headquartersLocation (3.1-dev) can add the producer's country.

NATIVE. An instance of Core/Relationship with relationshipType dependsOn: from = the dependent component, to = the dependencies (one or many). Verify edge direction. Use completeness (complete / incomplete / noAssertion) to state whether the dependency list is complete (Coverage) and LifecycleScopedRelationship.scope for build- vs runtime-only dependencies. 'Includes' relationships use relationshipType contains; separate SBOM documents for subcomponents are linked via SpdxDocument.import / ExternalMap or ExternalRef type bom.
CISA's 'a component includes another component' reading: Relationship with relationshipType contains from the containing package to its subcomponents. closeMatch.

A Relationship with relationshipType descendantOf (from = the derived component, to = the component it was largely derived from) carries the largely-derived-from reading of the CISA element. closeMatch.

NATIVE with artifact rule. Package.verifiedUsing (0..*) -> Core/Hash; Hash.hashValue (1..1) is the hexadecimal digest of the exact distributed executable artifact (hash the artifact, not a source directory or aggregate verification code). If the artifact is unavailable, state that the value is unknown in Hash.comment or omit with an Element.comment.
Artifact.verifiedUsing -> Hash is the algorithm + hashValue pair that contains this element. broadMatch (container).

NATIVE. Hash.algorithm (1..1) from the HashAlgorithm vocabulary (sha256, sha384, sha512, sha3_256, sha3_512, blake2b512, blake3, md5, sha1, ...). Values are SPDX identifiers, not IANA Hash Function Textual Names; the correspondence is deterministic (sha256 <-> 'sha-256'). Use an approved algorithm.
Artifact.verifiedUsing -> Hash is the algorithm + hashValue pair that contains this element. broadMatch (container).

NATIVE with version-specific vocabulary. Software/Package.packageUrl (0..1) carries the PURL (ECMA-427), the preferred common identifier. Include all available identifiers; local spdxId values do not replace common external identifiers.
ExternalIdentifier with externalIdentifierType cpe22 (identifier = the CPE 2.2 string). closeMatch (one identifier kind).
ExternalIdentifier with externalIdentifierType cpe23. closeMatch (one identifier kind).
ExternalIdentifier with externalIdentifierType swid (SWID tag id). closeMatch (one identifier kind).
ExternalIdentifier with externalIdentifierType swhid (Software Heritage persistent identifier). closeMatch (one identifier kind).
ExternalIdentifier with externalIdentifierType gitoid (OmniBOR artifact or input-manifest identifier). closeMatch (one identifier kind).

SoftwareArtifact.contentIdentifier (0..*) -> ContentIdentifier {contentIdentifierType: gitoid | swhid, contentIdentifierValue} for intrinsic, content-derived identifiers (OmniBOR gitoid, SWHID / ISO/IEC 18670). closeMatch (subset).
The element's spdxId IRI is globally unique and can be used as an identifier (e.g. a UUID URN), but CISA 2026 asks for common software identifiers in addition. closeMatch.

NATIVE. Relationship with relationshipType hasDeclaredLicense from the Package to an AnyLicenseInfo element: a SimpleLicensing/LicenseExpression (SPDX expression with license identifiers), ExpandedLicensing/ListedLicense or CustomLicense (proprietary terms, with licenseText or seeAlso URL). Use NoAssertionLicense when the license is unknown; NoneLicense when there is none. Model text: hasDeclaredLicense = license info the Artifact was discovered to contain; hasConcludedLicense = license the data creator concludes governs it. CISA's 'license(s) under which the component is available' may be carried by either; if both are present and differ, explain in comment.

SimpleLicensing/LicenseExpression.licenseExpression (1..1) carries the machine-processable license identifier expression; customIdToUri (renamed customIdToLicense in 3.1) maps LicenseRef identifiers to the license elements that hold the full text. closeMatch (value field of the relationship target).

NATIVE. Software/Package.name (Element.name, 1..1 on Package) preserves the producer's full name. GAP (cardinality): CISA 2026 asks formats to allow multiple entries for alternate names; Element.name is single-valued (spdx/spdx-3-model#1432); carry aliases as ExternalIdentifier / ExternalRef or in comment.
Software/Package.packageVersion (0..1) carries the component version string. Exact match. (SPDX 3.1 deprecates it in favour of Core/version on Package.)

Practice, not a data field. Relationship.completeness (RelationshipCompleteness: complete, incomplete, noAssertion) states whether the listed dependsOn / contains targets are the complete set, which lets a recipient conclude that an unlisted component is absent. Linked SBOMs for subcomponents: SpdxDocument.import (ExternalMap) and ExternalRef type bom.

Practice, not a data field. SPDX distinguishes unknown from absent: the NoAssertionElement / NoneElement individuals (and NoAssertionLicense / NoneLicense for licenses) as relationship targets, Relationship.completeness noAssertion, and PresenceType noAssertion on AI/Dataset properties. Withheld (redacted) information has no dedicated marker; use Element.comment.

column2: Accommodation of Updates to SBOM Data
column8: Practice, not a data field. Corrections are issued as a new Sbom/SpdxDocument revision (new spdxId, created, Bom.version) linked from the previous one with amendedBy. relatedMatch. Note: the RelationshipType vocabulary says the from Element is amended by each to Element (previous -> new), while the Bom class text says the Relationship goes from the updated BOM to the original; the model contradicts itself.

Practice, not a data field. SpdxDocument.dataLicense (0..1, AnyLicenseInfo; CC0-1.0 by SPDX convention) states the terms under which the SBOM data itself may be shared, the only format construct that touches access control; delivery with the installation, via a version-specific URL, an API or a repository is outside the model, the document being a self-contained serialisation. relatedMatch.

Practice, not a data field. Each build or release gets its own Sbom / SpdxDocument; a Relationship with relationshipType amendedBy from the previous document to the revised one records corrections and newly discovered details (see accommodation-of-updates). relatedMatch.

Practice, not a data field. CreationInfo.created (1..1) on each document, read together with the component versions the document describes, lets a consumer check that a new build or release came with a new SBOM. relatedMatch.

Practice, not a data field. SPDX (ISO/IEC 5962:2021 for 2.x) is one of the two machine-processable formats the practice names; the SpdxDocument element is the serialisation unit (JSON-LD with the published @context). relatedMatch.
Practice, not a data field. CreationInfo.specVersion (1..1) identifies the format version, which lets a consumer refuse deprecated format versions as the practice asks. relatedMatch.
